questions.prompt:
What exact output does code example 1 in this lesson produce?

whole = int('12')
ratio = float('0.5')
print(whole + 2, ratio)
print(int(3.9), round(3.9), bool('False'))
questions.explanation:
LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`whole = int('12')` — Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
`ratio = float('0.5')` — Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
`print(whole + 2, ratio)` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.
`print(int(3.9), round(3.9), bool('False'))` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.
